model_system: BRCA2-deficient and BRCA2-complemented isogenic cell lines (V-C8 hamster, human); clonogenic survival
dose_and_schedule: PARP inhibitor (NU1025 / AG14361 class) continuous in vitro exposure
mechanism: PARP inhibition leaves unrepaired single-strand breaks that collapse replication forks into double-strand breaks; cells lacking BRCA2 cannot repair these by homologous recombination and die.
key_finding: BRCA2-deficient cells were several orders of magnitude more sensitive to PARP inhibition than their BRCA2-proficient counterparts, with no DNA-damaging agent added. This was one of the two 2005 papers that defined the BRCA-PARP synthetic-lethal interaction.
caveats: In-vitro mechanism paper, not an ovarian model. It underpins the entire PARP-inhibitor maintenance rationale that gates this case, which is why it is kept despite no in-vivo ovarian arm. Relevance to this patient is conditional on the pending tumor HRD/somatic-BRCA result.

exclusion_reason: Companion 2005 mechanism paper to Bryant et al.; same BRCA-PARP synthetic-lethal finding in isogenic cell lines. Logged as the second co-discovery but not separately synthesized to avoid double-counting the same in-vitro concept.

model_system: patient-derived ovarian serous carcinoma tissue xenograft, BRCA2 germline-mutated (vs a BRCA-proficient serous xenograft)
control_arm: vehicle; plus BRCA-proficient serous xenograft as specificity control
dose_and_schedule: olaparib 50 mg/kg/day, alone and combined with carboplatin
mechanism: Olaparib exploits the homologous-recombination defect of BRCA2-mutant tumor cells, and carboplatin adds interstrand crosslinks that the same defective repair machinery cannot resolve.
key_finding: Olaparib inhibited growth of the BRCA2-mutant ovarian PDX, and the carboplatin combination either eradicated tumors or left only scar tissue on histology. A BRCA-proficient serous xenograft showed no olaparib effect, fixing the response to the BRCA2 defect.
caveats: Closest preclinical match to this tumor type: a BRCA2-mutant ovarian serous PDX with a proficient control. Single PDX per genotype limits generalization. Case match is partial because the patient's germline BRCA is wild-type and her tumor HRD/somatic-BRCA status is still pending.

model_system: BRCA-mutant and BRCA-wild-type tumor xenografts (incl. intracranial TNBC); comparative PK across PARP inhibitors
control_arm: vehicle; head-to-head vs olaparib at matched MTD
dose_and_schedule: niraparib oral daily at maximum tolerated dose; compared with olaparib
mechanism: Niraparib distributes into tumor tissue well above plasma, sustaining intratumoral PARP trapping and synthetic lethality in HR-deficient cells and producing growth inhibition even in BRCA-wild-type tumors.
key_finding: Steady-state tumor exposure to niraparib was about 3.3x plasma, the inverse of olaparib's tumor-to-plasma ratio. Niraparib gave stronger tumor growth inhibition than olaparib at matched MTD, including in BRCA-wild-type models.
caveats: PK/efficacy comparison across tumor types rather than a dedicated ovarian study. The tumor-penetration advantage supports niraparib's clinical benefit in HRD-uncertain and BRCA-wild-type disease (PRIMA all-comers), which matters here because the patient's HRD score is pending.

exclusion_reason: Rucaparib (AG-014699/CO-338) preclinical activity in BRCA-mutant/HR-deficient xenografts duplicates the PARP synthetic-lethal mechanism already covered by the olaparib and niraparib rows. Kept as audit trail; not separately synthesized.

model_system: orthotopic syngeneic mouse model of end-stage epithelial ovarian carcinoma (ID8-derived)
mechanism: Sustained VEGF neutralization restrains tumor angiogenesis and ascites-driving vascular permeability in disseminated ovarian carcinoma.
key_finding: Sustained bevacizumab expression extended survival in an orthotopic ovarian model and gave the largest single-agent survival gain among the antiangiogenic agents tested. The benefit held even in the end-stage disease setting.
caveats: Orthotopic syngeneic ovarian model is a good tissue match, but delivery is AAV-vectored continuous expression rather than the IV q3w antibody the patient receives, so dose kinetics differ. Supports the anti-angiogenic axis she is already on.

exclusion_reason: Ovarian xenograft work, but the endpoint is bevacizumab-induced vessel normalization reducing antibody uptake (a drug-delivery caution), not antitumor efficacy against the patient's targetable VEGF axis. Mechanistically tangential to the maintenance decision.

model_system: ovariectomized BALB/c nude mice, peritoneal carcinomatosis of ERalpha-positive OVCAR-3 vs ERalpha-low DISS
mechanism: Aromatase inhibition lowers local estrogen, downregulating ERalpha and FOXP1 signaling and cutting tumor VEGF, so the antitumor effect tracks ERalpha expression and runs partly through reduced angiogenesis.
key_finding: Letrozole prolonged survival in ERalpha-positive OVCAR-3 carcinomatosis but not in ERalpha-low DISS tumors. Tumor microvessel density fell to 5.8 vs 8.9 vessels/mm2 and VEGF dropped, while caspase-3 apoptosis was unchanged.
caveats: ERalpha-dependence of the effect matches the patient's ER-positive biology, but OVCAR-3 is a high-ER line whereas her ER is weak-to-moderate intensity and PR-negative, tempering expected magnitude. Effect appears antiangiogenic/cytostatic rather than cytotoxic.

model_system: CT-26 subcutaneous syngeneic tumors, BALB/c mice (water-soluble lipopolymer / IL-12 plasmid)
dose_and_schedule: intratumoral WSLP-p2CMVmIL-12 complex, repeated at 4-day vs 8-day intervals
mechanism: A polymer-condensed IL-12 plasmid produces local, sustained IL-12 with limited systemic spillover, driving IFN-gamma and a cytotoxic-T-cell response against the tumor.
key_finding: Repeated lipopolymer/IL-12 dosing at 4-day intervals gave maximal tumor suppression and survival, beating less frequent dosing. The formulation kept IL-12 local and limited systemic distribution, the design rationale carried into GEN-1/IMNN-001.
caveats: Foundational lipopolymer/IL-12 proof-of-concept for the GEN-1 platform, but in a colon (CT-26) subcutaneous model, not ovarian. Later murine pmIL-12/PPC ID8 ovarian work (intraperitoneal, IL-12/IFN-gamma induction with reduced ascitic VEGF) extends this to the patient's tissue but is reported mainly in review/secondary form. Cross-tumor only.
